# Patterns for the privacy guard.
#
# One file, sourced by .github/ci/check-privacy.sh, which the git hooks and the
# CI workflow both call. A guard that exists in two places and is updated in one
# is worse than no guard.
#
# Why this exists: a tracked document once referred, in ordinary English, to
# private material eight times. Every path-based check passed it, because the
# leak was wording rather than a filename. Paths alone do not catch that.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SELF-REFERENCE
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The guard scans tracked files, and two of them have to contain the words it
# searches for in order to function. Both are excluded from the vocabulary scan
# only, and both are listed here so the exclusion is a decision on the record
# rather than a gap nobody notices:
#
#   .github/ci/**   this file, and the script that reads it
#   .gitignore      must name the local-only directories in order to exclude them
#
# Neither is excluded from review, and neither is excluded from the local-path
# scan. If you add a third file that must contain these words, name it here.
EXCLUDE_VOCAB='.github/ci,.gitignore'
EXCLUDE_PATHS='.github/ci'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vocabulary
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scheduling nouns that indicate prose referring to private material.
#
# Word-bounded on non-alphanumeric characters, so ordinary words that merely
# contain these as substrings are not flagged: planned, planner, planes,
# programmer.
#
# The boundary class also excludes "/", so a legitimate directory that happens
# to be named "plan" is not flagged. Referring to a plan in prose is the finding;
# a path segment is not. A path-shaped reference is caught by PATH_PATTERN below.
PATTERN='[Pp]lanning|(^|[^[:alnum:]/])[Pp]lans?([^[:alnum:]/]|$)|[Rr]oadmap|(^|[^[:alnum:]/])[Pp]hases?([^[:alnum:]/]|$)|[Mm]ilestone'

# A local checkout path, the local overlay filename, a drive-qualified path to
# private material, or a bare path-shaped reference to a private document.
#
# The last alternative catches "see plan/01.md" written in prose, which the
# vocabulary pattern deliberately allows because the word is a path segment.
PATH_PATTERN="[A-Za-z]:[\\\\/]Us[e]rs[\\\\/]|VsCode[/\\\\]a[x]|agent[-]brief|[A-Za-z]:[/\\\\]plan|(^|[[:space:]\"'(])[Pp]lan[/\\\\]"

# Local-only directories and files, matched as paths.
LOCAL_PATH_PATTERN='^(plan|\.scratch|\.ax|docs/agents)/|^AGENTS\.md$|(^|/)CONTEXT\.local\.md$|\.internal\.'
